title: Choosing where to run a job
description: A short decision exercise: compare providers for several jobs and choose one for each.

start.heading: Before you begin
intro: You will see {count} short tasks. For each task, several providers could run the job. Choose the one you would use.
There are no trick questions. Your answers are kept in this browser only. Nothing is sent to a server. At the end you can download your answers as a file.
start.pidHint: If the researcher gave you a code, enter it here. Do not enter your name.

card.estimatesNote: Electricity, water and carbon are estimates for this one job. Water is allocated by compute share: an accounting estimate, not measured consumption.

demoNotice: Demo data only. These values are illustrative and are not provider claims.

done.heading: Finished
body: Thank you. Your answers are in this browser only. Nothing has been sent.
Download the results file and send it to the researcher who asked you to take part.

design.heading: Design of the exercise (researchers)
design.intro: Every figure below is computed from the inputs in content/experiment/trials.json by the transaction accounting module. The same numbers can be downloaded for the simulation.
design.correct: Correct option = lowest facility energy per transaction. Ties are all correct. Water-lowest and carbon-lowest are listed separately. "Agree" is unknown when an option has no water figure.

receipt.heading: Transaction receipt (sample)
receipt.intro: A receipt for one job, built by the same accounting module. The job and the provider are a demo. The values are computed from the inputs shown here.
receipt.sampleNote: Demo data only. This is not a record of a real job.

allocationValues.reserved-share: reserved share of shared GPU capacity, times time

powerScopeValues.it-only: IT equipment only (cooling and overhead added through PUE)

receipt.hashNote: Both hashes are taken over canonical JSON (RFC 8785): keys sorted, no whitespace. The receipt hash does not change if the file is re-formatted. The source hash can be recomputed by anyone who holds the source data file. Neither hash shows that the provider's sensors or reported figures are accurate.
receipt.signIntro: The provider signs the receipt with a wallet. The signature is an EAS off-chain attestation (EIP-712). Nothing is sent to the blockchain and it costs no gas. It signs the two hashes above and the method name.
receipt.signWhat: The signature shows who issued the receipt and that it was not altered afterwards. It does not show that the provider's sensors or figures are correct.
receipt.signTestNote: Try it with a test wallet. The attester is the connected wallet. Do not use a wallet that holds real assets for this demo.
receipt.recipientLabel: Recipient wallet address (the person the job ran for)
receipt.recipientInvalid: This is not a valid address. Check the characters and the upper/lower case.
receipt.recipientChecksum: The upper/lower case does not match the address checksum. Check for a typo.
receipt.connectFirst: Connect a wallet first (button in the header).
receipt.signSwitch: The wallet must be on Sepolia to sign. Please switch the network.
receipt.signedDone: Signed. Download the file and hand it to the recipient.
receipt.easscanNote: The easscan page reads the signature from the link itself. The schema is not registered on Sepolia yet, so easscan may not show the schema name.
receipt.verifyIntro: Choose a signed receipt file. The check runs in this browser. It needs no wallet and sends nothing.
receipt.verifySourceHelp: If you also choose the source data file, its hash is recomputed and compared.
receipt.verifyOk: All checks passed. The file was signed by the attester below and has not been altered.
receipt.verifyNg: Some checks failed. Do not rely on this file.
receipt.verifyCaveat: This does not show that the provider's sensors or figures are correct.

checks.wellFormed: The file has the form of a signed receipt
checks.receiptHashMatches: The receipt hash equals the signed value
checks.sourceHashMatches: The source hash in the receipt equals the signed value
checks.methodMatches: The method name equals the signed value
checks.schemaMatches: The schema is the expected one
checks.uidMatches: The attestation ID matches its content
checks.signatureMatches: The signature was made by the attester shown

receipt.sourceCheck: Source data file: its hash equals the one in the receipt
receipt.sourceCheckNg: Source data file: its hash does NOT equal the one in the receipt
